name: OH-14
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent David Joyce running with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger underfunded with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: Joyce holds a strong structural advantage: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and a massive fundraising edge over an underfunded challenger. Prediction markets price a Republican win near 94%, and no polls or expert ratings suggest movement toward the Democrat.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending or unexpectedly strong Democratic fundraising could narrow the margin, though nothing currently signals that.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
David Joyce, the Republican incumbent, is favored to win another term in this northeastern Ohio district, which leans Republican by about ten points. He has raised over $1.4 million and holds more than $3.1 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Maria Jukic has raised only about $62,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Joyce.

Prediction markets give Joyce roughly a 94% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the stark financial gap, all of which point to a comfortable Republican win with modest residual uncertainty.
